slices.focus: Ayaka finally tells her sister Eri why she stays in terminal work — not from habit or guilt, but because service failures affect real households — shifting their dynamic.
slices.summary: After avoiding the conversation all summer, Ayaka tells her sister Eri directly that the work feels personal — she thinks about households waiting on groceries and medicine, not just job stress. Eri shifts from pushing for a mainland office job to asking how Ayaka is actually holding up. Ayaka gives Eri concrete ways to help: check on meals, sleep, whether she needs to vent. The relationship becomes less prickly and more supportive.
open_loops: Eri may revert to old patterns during Ayaka's next rough stretch
